notifications.title: Notifications

notifications.ownPhoneMissing: Your phone was not found: it is not in your person in Home Assistant (Settings → People). Add it there or choose among other devices.
notifications.automatic: Chosen automatically: the phones of your person in Home Assistant.
notifications.testSentHint: Check your phone and notifications in Home Assistant.

language.title: Language
language.hint: The language of the app and notifications. When following the browser, Home Assistant notifications come in the language of Home Assistant itself.

register.title: New account

login.homeAssistantHint: Sign in once — after that Home Assistant signs you in
login.hint: Sign in to see this month's report

instruments.title: Instruments & quotes
instruments.historyFailed: Could not load the quote history.
instruments.noQuotes: No quotes for the period — update the quotes.
instruments.chooseInstrumentHint: Price chart, change over the period, high, low and volatility.
instruments.subtitle: Closing prices every night at 22:30 (Mon–Fri)
instruments.subtitleWithLast: Closing prices every night at 22:30 (Mon–Fri) · latest — {date}

backtest.title: How the strategy behaved in the past
backtest.computingHint: Computing in the background, this may take a few minutes
backtest.notSupported: This strategy does not support testing on history.
backtest.yourMoney: What would have happened to your money
backtest.disclaimer: With your parameters, {start} – {end}. These are past results, not a forecast: with today’s list of instruments, so the real result will likely be worse. The “After tax” column counts tax by the default tax policy: the strategy pays it every year on gains from sales, and the comparison once, when everything is sold at the end. Tax on dividends is not counted.
backtest.tooLittleHistory: Too little history for segments of {count, plural, one {# year} other {# years}}.
backtest.fewPeriods: There are few of them, so the range may be too narrow.

tiles.freeCashHint: The broker keeps cash separately in each currency; other currencies here are at the current official rate

summary.unrealizedHint: unrealised result of the open positions
summary.priceHint: Prices are the exchange close of the last trading day, currencies the official rate. The broker’s app (Revolut) shows the current price and its own market rate, so the amount may differ by a few tenths of a percent.

sleeve.shareInAccount: share of the account {actual} with a target of {target}

holdings.title: Holdings
holdings.staleQuotes: Some quotes are stale or missing — the value of those positions may be inaccurate.
holdings.emptyHint: Import positions.json on the account page or mark executions in a report.
holdings.subtitleAll: All accounts together in {currency} (official rate) · FIFO lots per sub-portfolio
holdings.subtitle: Virtual FIFO lots per sub-portfolio by the latest quotes

strategies.unused: Not used anywhere yet — choose it in an account sub-portfolio

picker.noneHint: The sub-portfolio just holds what it has; reports leave it alone.

strategies.savedHint: Sub-portfolios that follow the latest version use it from the next report

blurb.reportPoint: A report with buys and sells — whenever suits you: you set the schedule in the account
blurb.riskSells: Between rebalances checks the risk: sells only on an exit signal
blurb.riskWarns: Between rebalances checks the risk: single positions only warn, while selling the whole portfolio stays
blurb.picks: Picks the {topN} strongest of {count} {region} ETFs and holds them equally
blurb.holds: Holds {count} {region} ETFs equally, whatever the market does
blurb.correlation: Skips a fund that moves too much like one already chosen (correlation above {limit})
blurb.volatilityCash: When the chosen funds swing more than {target}% a year, keeps part of the money in {cash}
blurb.volatilityNoCash: When the chosen funds swing more than {target}% a year, keeps part of the money in cash
blurb.weakMarketCash: Weak market: invests {share}% of the contribution, the rest goes to {cash}
blurb.weakMarket: Weak market: invests {share}% of the contribution

detail.signalDeleted: The strategy relies on a deleted signal. Change it in the builder; reports whose rules use this signal are not made.
detail.archiveHint: No new versions can be created; reports that refer to it stay.
detail.subtitle: {type} · engine {engine} {version}

list.subtitle: A strategy decides which ETFs to hold in a sub-portfolio and how often to review; the service works out what to buy and sell
list.emptyHint: Start with the defaults: adaptive momentum and index holding for European ETFs and for US ones. Parameters can be changed any time, each change is a new version.

value.gainOverContributed: gain over what was contributed · contributed
value.gainOnAssets: gain on assets · paid for them
value.planVsActualHint: — the difference from “if everything went to plan”. Dots on the line are report days.
value.title: Value of {scope} · {date}
value.gainOnAssetsHint: How much the assets you hold are worth now above what was paid for them with fees. Free cash and what was already sold are not included — this is the same result as on the “Holdings” page.

tax.title: Tax
tax.redAboveThreshold: In red — above the threshold: {share} of the current value of all accounts.

allocation.singleHint: Here the actual share of each sub-portfolio is compared with its target. You have one sub-portfolio (target 100%), so there is nothing to compare — see the instruments in

metrics.twrHint: How the strategy worked, regardless of when and how much you contributed. For comparing with indices and funds.
metrics.xirrHint: The yearly return of your own money — counting the dates and amounts of contributions and withdrawals.
metrics.drawdownHint: How far the value is now below its highest peak (without the effect of contributions).

details.currencyHint: Amounts are in {currency} at each day’s official rate; an account’s TWR is in its own currency.
details.exitSignals: {count, plural, one {# exit signal} other {# exit signals}}

overview.setupTitle: Let’s start: set up your account
overview.setupHint: In a few steps: which broker you use, how to split the money, which strategy to choose and how much to invest each month. The default strategies are ready — each step explains what and why.
overview.noTransactions: Charts appear with the first transaction in the journal: import positions or mark a contribution in a report.
overview.taxAlert: Tax {taxYear} — {taxDue}, that is {ratio} of the value of all accounts: above the threshold of {share} ({limit}).
overview.noStrategy: No sub-portfolio has a strategy — reports will not know what to buy.
overview.noStrategyOfAccount: {account}: no sub-portfolio has a strategy — reports will not know what to buy.
overview.reportWaiting: Report for {period}: {open} of {total} actions wait to be marked.

notifications.title: Which signals to notify about
notifications.hint: A new signal notifies by itself until you turn it off here.

editor.deleteHint: Its history goes with it, and connected reports will no longer start.
editor.name: Name
editor.peakWindow: Look for the peak over, days
editor.quotesDaily: Quotes update once a day at 22:30, so checking more often sees the same data.
editor.noReports: None yet. Strategies do not know about the signal: it is the same report, only earlier.
editor.afterCreate: Notifications turn on by themselves. Reports can be connected once the signal is created.

signals.subtitle: They watch the market and your portfolio and tell you when a condition fires
signals.noneActive: No signal is firing right now.
signals.emptyHint: Built-in signals appear as soon as there is an account. You can also create your own.

realizations.title: Realisations (sales)
realizations.revolutDiffers: Revolut counts a gain of {brokerGainInTaxCurrency} (difference {brokerGainInTaxCurrency2}): it has its own rate and rounding, we use the official rate of the day before the trade.
realizations.withoutPurchase: {quantity} sh. without a purchase in the journal — the cost is zero

brokerStatements.deleteHint: Dividend tax will again be counted without crediting what was withheld abroad, and cost will no longer come from the statement.
brokerStatements.title: Broker statement (P&L)
brokerStatements.hint: Revolut → brokerage account → Documents → profit and loss statement (PDF). It gives the tax withheld from dividends abroad (it reduces the Polish one), the cost of shares without a purchase in the journal (for example after a spin-off) and Revolut’s gain for checking. Transactions are still imported from CSV.
brokerStatements.unmatched: the rest found no transaction in the journal — import the CSV for the same period

losses.title: Past years’ losses
losses.hint: Yours, not an account’s: one entry per year for all brokers.
losses.deleteHint: The loss of {year} will no longer reduce the tax.

dividends.title: Dividends
dividends.withholdingUnknown: The tax withheld abroad is unknown, so the tax is counted from the received amount without a credit. Upload the broker’s P&L statement below.

declaration.cheatSheetHint: One page: what goes where in e-Urząd, with poz. numbers
declaration.onFormHint: The official PIT-38 and PIT/ZG forms with the amounts filled in — for paper
declaration.draftHint: A draft for e-Urząd Skarbowy / Twój e-PIT. Check the amounts against the PIT-8C and the brokers’ statements; in disputed cases, with a tax adviser.
declaration.subtitle: {title} · file from 15 February to {deadline}
declaration.pit8cCoveredBy: PIT-8C — one per broker, entered on “{pit8CCoveredBy}”
declaration.title: Declaration

taxes.removePit8cHint: The broker’s proceeds and costs in the declaration will again be counted from your transactions, not from its PIT-8C.
taxes.emptyHint: Tax appears with the first sale or dividend. Purchases already form FIFO lots.

due.title: Tax to pay · {year}
due.accountsTogether: · {count, plural, one {# account} other {# accounts}} together
due.formHint: {title}: all your accounts together, field by field, and a PDF on the form

trade.title: Record a trade
trade.autoSplitHint: Without a choice: a buy is split by target shares, a sell by the units held.

upload.title: Import into account
upload.drop: Choose or drop a Revolut CSV statement here
upload.hint: In the Revolut app: brokerage account → documents → account statement, CSV format. Nothing is recorded until you confirm.
upload.pnlHint: Tax withheld from dividends abroad and the cost of shares after a spin-off are only in the P&L statement (PDF) — upload it on the page

rows.nothingNew: The statement has no new transactions: everything is already in the journal.
rows.confirmMessage: {count} transactions will be recorded. The import can be undone in one step.
rows.confirmMessageWithReversals: {count} transactions will be recorded, {reversed} reversed. The import can be undone in one step.

import.cancelledHint: The transactions it recorded were reversed
import.cancelHint: All transactions recorded by this import will be reversed.
import.fileLine: {fileName} · {rows, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}} · account in {accountCurrency}

mode.OverwriteHint: All previous imports (statements and positions.json) will be reversed, and the statement imported again. Manual transactions and marks from reports stay.

import.subtitle: The account statement (CSV) becomes records in the journal of account “{account}”: trades, top-ups, withdrawals, dividends

ledger.reverseHint: The original stays in the journal, and the reversal cancels its effect on positions, cash and taxes.
ledger.subtitle: Positions and cash derive from these records; records do not change — a reversal fixes a mistake
ledger.emptyHint: Transactions appear when you mark actions in a report, import positions.json or record a trade by hand.
ledger.undoneByReport: Undone by a mark in the report

mode.AppendHint: Only new rows are added. Uploading the same or a fresher statement again duplicates nothing.
mode.UpdateHint: Like “Append”, and rows imported earlier with other figures are overwritten from the statement (reversal + a new record).
mode.FromScratchHint: The whole account journal is reversed, then the statement is imported. Use it if you start the bookkeeping over.
